provenance: T-M32-13, found on `task/M32` when PR #34 went red on CI and diagnosed to root cause there; T-R44 carries the fix. `evals/run.py` stamped every ledger row with `time.strftime("%Y%m%d-%H%M%S")` — naive local time, no zone — and ADR-019 §6 item 2 (cited-run)'s dirty allowance orders those strings as if they were real time (`r["ts"] <= ts`, "was a clean row already available when this band was published?"). The committed ledger mixes zones: this laptop writes Asia/Taipei, a runner writes UTC. The band row `20260823-192533` is 11:25:33Z; CI's `invariant` row `20260823-115044` is 11:50:44Z — 25 minutes LATER in real time, eight hours EARLIER as a string. CI's row is clean, because a fresh checkout makes `git_dirty()` false, so it disqualified a dirty citation it did not predate — and a dirty citation is unavoidable when a case is added, since the tree only reaches count N+1 while the new case is uncommitted. That is what made every case addition cost two commits. `evals/run.py` `stamp()` is UTC now. This case grades the ORDERING property; `band-is-graded-against-its-own-environment` grades the environment one. They are two different claims and neither substitutes for the other: UTC makes `ts` a valid key, and a foreign-environment row is still the wrong row to derive a ceiling from whatever its stamp says — ADR-019 §7 says so in those words. The two zones are set explicitly with `TZ` + `time.tzset()` rather than inherited from the host: a check that asked the machine what time it is would be red on this laptop and GREEN on a UTC runner, which is the environment-dependent shape `fast-wall-clock-budget` was falsified by twice (PR #20 R1, and again when CI's own override made the case's assertion wrong). The pair is re-derived from its two real instants rather than quoted as two strings, so the fixture cannot drift from what it claims to represent.

triage.note: tagged invariant and fast, like the rest of the band subsystem. Costs nothing: two `tzset` calls and one `_band_wrong` over a two-row synthetic ledger, no network, no spend. `time.tzset()` is POSIX-only, which is every platform this repo runs on (macOS locally, ubuntu-latest on CI); it would raise on Windows and the runner would report that as a case failure rather than a silent pass. What this case does NOT grade, and ADR-019 §7 states as an assumption instead: that the committed ledger holds no pre-switch local-stamped row at a live case count. It is true of this tree — this commit's own two cases moved both counts, so every row at 155/60 was written after the switch — but it is not gradeable from the ledger, because a row does not record the zone it was written in and a `ts` threshold cannot separate the sides: a post-switch UTC stamp sorts BELOW a pre-switch local stamp of the same day. A threshold would have been green on a ledger that still mixed zones.
triage.watched_red: Watched red against the local stamping that shipped, with `stamp()` extracted verbatim from `main()` first so there was a surface to grade and no behaviour had yet changed. All three assertions fired at once: [{same_instant_stamped_differently_per_zone: {'Asia/Taipei': '20260823-192533', 'UTC': '20260823-112533'}}, {later_run_sorts_earlier: {earlier_instant: '20260823-192533', later_instant: '20260823-115044'}}, {dirty_clause_fired_on_a_row_that_came_later: [{suite: 's', cited_a_dirty_run: '20260823-192533', clean_runs_available_by_then: ['20260823-115044']}]}]. The second and third reproduce T-M32-13's own pair exactly, from the two real instants rather than from quoted strings, and the third shows the clause that consumed it. Green after `stamp()` moved to `time.gmtime`. A fourth assertion was written and REMOVED before shipping, which is the finding worth keeping: it graded that no live case count holds a row older than the UTC switch, against a `_BAND_TS_UTC_SINCE = "20260823-140000"` threshold. It passed — and it passed for the wrong reason. Post-switch UTC stamps that day are `20260823-14xxxx` and the pre-switch local rows at the same case count are `20260823-21xxxx`, so the pre-switch rows sort ABOVE the boundary and the threshold cleared them. A check that is green on exactly the state it exists to refuse is worse than no check, so the assumption is stated in ADR-019 §7 and the code says why it is not graded. Two more, after the fix. The stamp reverted to `time.localtime` reddens all three assertions again with the same payload, which is the mutation that holds this case up. And the design decision was falsified from the other side: replacing the two explicit `stamped(tz, …)` calls with bare `_run.stamp(…)` — zones inherited from the host — returns GREEN. It would return green under the bug too, on any UTC runner, which is exactly the environment-dependent shape the provenance describes; the case sets `TZ` for that reason and not for tidiness.
